project.title: Monosaccharide and disaccharide
project.projectDescription: Proteins from Hela cells were captured by monosaccharide and disaccharide probes. Resulting proteins were went through proteomics. Unique proteins from disaccharide samples were selected for further research.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: On beads trypsin digestion   Beads were diluted with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate. The samples were treated with 4 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) for 15 min at 65 °C and 10 mM chloroacetamide (CAA) in the dark for 30 min at room temperature. Then, beads were digested with 500 ng trypsin overnight at 37 °C. Tryptic peptides were desalted with ZipTip using the manufacture protocol (MilliporeSigma, Temecula, CA, USA). The peptides were lyophilized to dryness at 160 mBar using a labconco speedvac (Centrivap, Labconco Inc., USA). Peptides derived from protein digests were resuspended in 0.1% formic acid (FA) for LC-MS analysis. Three biological replicates for each genotype were prepared for proteomics.      Liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry for proteomics   Proteomics data acquisition was carried out on EASY-nLC™ 1200 System (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., San Jose, CA, USA) coupled with Orbitrap Fusion™ Mass Spectrometers (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc., San Jose, CA, USA). Samples were loaded onto an Acclaim PepMap® 100 C18 trapping column (75 μm i.d. × 2 cm, 3 μm, 100 Å) and then separated on a PepMap® C18 analytical column (75 μm i.d. × 25 cm, 2 μm, 100 Å). The flow rate was set at 250 nL/min with solvent A (0.1% FA in water) and solvent B (0.1% FA and 80% ACN in water) as the mobile phase. Separation was conducted using the following gradient: 2 – 35% of B over 0 – 70 min; 35 – 80% of B over 70 – 75 min; 80 – 98% of B over 75 – 76 min, and isocratic at 98% of B over 76 – 90 min.   For MS data acquisition, the full MS1 scan (m/z 350 - 1800) was performed on the Orbitrap with a resolution of 120,000. The automatic gain control (AGC) target is 2e5 with 50 ms as the maximum injection time (MIT). Peptides bearing +2 – 6 charges were selected with an intensity threshold of 1e20. dynamic exclusion of 30 s was used to prevent resampling the high abundance peptides. The MS/MS was carried out in the Orbitrap with a quadrupole isolation window of 1.3 Da. Fragmentation of the top 10 selected peptides by Collision-induced dissociation (CID) was done at 35% of normalized collision energy. The MS2 spectra were acquired at a IonTrap with AGC target as 1e4 and the maximum injection time as 35 ms.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Proteome DiscovererTM (version 2.5, Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany) was used to search the MS/MS spectra from the protein samples. The SEQUEST algorithm in the Proteome Discoverer was used to process raw data files. Spectra were searched using the uniprot homo sapiens protein database with the following parameters: 10 ppm mass tolerance for MS1 and 0.02 as mass tolerance for MS2, two maximum missed tryptic cleavage sites, a fixed modification of carbamidomethylation (+57.021) on cysteine residues, dynamic modifications of oxidation of methionine (+15.996). Search results were filtered at 1% false discovery rate (FDR) and at least two unique peptides per protein for protein identification. Relative protein abundance in the samples was measured using label-free quantification. Proteins identified and quantified in all the four biological samples were used, and no imputation was performed. Peptides in samples were quantified as area under the chromatogram peak. FDR cutoffs for both peptide and protein identification were set as 1%.
